newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam slams banks over debt.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam slams banks over debt.

text.p: Vietnam's official Communist Party newspaper, the Nhan Dan daily, accused the country's banks Thursday of incompetence and corruption, saying millions of dollars risked being lost through poor management of debt.
A hard-hitting and lengthy front-page editorial said as much as 42 percent of debt owed to state-owned commercial banks was overdue.
While the level of overdue payments to private banks was much lower, the quality of debt was so poor that as much as 50 percent might never be recovered, it said.

"The important thing is there is still a threat of something unusual, unhealthy and unsafe...hundreds of billions of Vietnam dong (millions of dollars) are doubtful debts -- big losses are likely," the newspaper said.
The article added that in addition to the potential losses, the carelessness with which credit was being managed was having a negative impact on society and fuelling corruption.
"Many disputes and credit violations have led to criminal cases, of which a number of banking cadres and officials have been prosecuted, judged and condemned," it said.
Vietnam's still nascent banking system has been criticised in a number of official newspapers in recent weeks, mostly over interest and credit policies.
The English-language Vietnam News reported Thursday that the State Bank of Vietnam had announced plans to control foreign loan activities to domestic enterprises through loan restrictions and quotas.
It said commercial banks had helped Vietnamese firms open letters of credit worth $1.2 billion with foreign creditors during the first eight months of this year.
But it said falling prices of some consumer goods had left enterprises unable to pay back their loans, leaving commercial banks liable for millions of dollars in overdue debt.
In Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's economic hub, the level of overdue debt amounted to $47 million in the first six months of this year, it added.
